correctness.rationale: Dimensionless killed backward PDE is derived from the exact stochastic dynamics with fully absorbing disk boundary. The first angular harmonic f_beta solves an inhomogeneous modified-Bessel equation; averaging the second-order Poisson equation and imposing regularity at the origin gives g_beta(rho)=1/2 integral_rho^1 f_beta(s)ds and the displayed formula. I1(z)/z monotonicity and a positivity-preserving radial Dirichlet inverse give strict sign and monotonicity in beta. Bessel ratio asymptotics yield distinct beta^-1 bulk and beta^-3/2 rim laws. Fixed-beta analytic expansion is even after heading averaging. The all-speed center comparison conditions on independent heading paths and applies Gaussian shift log-concavity plus Cameron-Martin analyticity; it is explicitly credited to Anderson. checker.py passed symbolic zero-beta ODE residuals, 42 independently integrated Bessel quadratures, a separate exact Green kernel at 5 drift speeds, fixed-interior and rim numerical asymptotic tests.

originality.rationale: Closest primary disk literature (Di Trapani et al. 2023) gives spectral propagator and survival but no closed isotropic mean second-speed derivative. A later paper (Iyaniwura and Peng 2025) explicitly derives exactly the first speed derivative and notes its cancellation under isotropic heading, without stating the quadratic response or rotational rim boundary layer. Prior known all-speed Gaussian comparison via Anderson is credited and not counted as novel. The claimed contribution is the exact leading isotropic response plus its nonuniform fast-reorientation classification, rather than the first-order mode, Gaussian comparison or generic Poisson PDE. This is an original claim under checked literature with residual priority risk.
residual_risks: A direct integration of the published q=2 spectral propagator or a subsequent unlocated paper may contain the exact quadratic coefficient implicitly or explicitly.

The 2025 first-order radial Bessel formula makes the second-order isotropic response derivable via one further radial Poisson problem; publication priority and contribution scale require external expert judgment.
The full original Anderson 1955 publisher PDF was inaccessible (HTTP 403); its theorem is standard and its use was checked from other descriptions, but it is contextual, not an originality basis.
The perturbation expansion is not jointly uniform in propulsion speed and divergent rotational diffusivity; no such claim is made.

value.rationale: For a physically natural orientation-uniform swimmer population, the entire known linear escape response cancels, making this exact quadratic coefficient the first measurable mean-exit sensitivity. The coefficient has a strict sign and ordering in rotational diffusivity over the entire interior, while its spatial high-rotation asymptotics are singular: O(beta^-1) in the bulk but O(beta^-3/2) at distance O(beta^-1/2) from the absorber. This explicitly separates persistence-length and geometric-boundary effects; the rim crossover is motivated by the natural fast-turning limit, not an arbitrary chosen parameter. It does not claim large-scale consequences beyond this exact physically interpretable response.
